- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or neutral (e.g., -0.28 or 0.00) — model tends to overshoot downward corrections.
- Underestimate downward moves when sentiment is mildly negative (e.g., -0.28) — model fails to anticipate sharp drops following recent highs.
- Overreact to short-term sentiment swings — model overcorrects on sentiment shifts, leading to exaggerated peaks or troughs.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high in the short term after strong upward moves, ignoring recent downward momentum.
- Lagged response to sentiment: model reacts to sentiment changes with a 1–2 day delay, causing misalignment with true price behavior.
- When sentiment is consistently low (e.g., 0.00 or negative), model tends to overestimate recovery — prices often bottom earlier than forecast.
- Avoid overconfidence in 30-day forecasts when sentiment is volatile — model exhibits higher variance in error when sentiment swings >0.30.
